name: Tanning mitt
lead: A tanning mitt is a thin glove, typically velvet-like on the outside and sometimes lined with latex or another barrier on the inside, used to spread self-tanning product across the skin and keep the user's hands from being coloured. It is a common accessory for applying sunless tanner, particularly to avoid stained palms. [1]

The mitt has no tanning action of its own. Colour comes from the sunless tanner, whose active ingredient, dihydroxyacetone (DHA), reacts with amino acids in surface skin cells. DHA is regulated by the FDA as a cosmetic color additive for external use, and reviews advise keeping it away from the eyes, lips and mucous membranes. [2][3]
No published study has tested tanning mitts. Statements that a mitt produces more even colour or prevents orange palms come from product use and community experience rather than trials.
infobox: Washable or replaceable; residue can build up

paras: Sunless tanners come as lotions, gels, mousses, sprays, wipes and drops. Applying them by hand leaves colour on the palms and between the fingers, because DHA also reacts with the keratin of the hands; a mitt separates the hand from the product. [1][2]

The mitt spreads product in a thin layer through a smoothing, circular motion, and a barrier lining blocks contact between the hand and product. This follows from how DHA behaves on skin, since the colour forms in the outermost dead skin layer. [1][2]
No studies found. Research on DHA itself is covered in reviews of sunless tanning, including a 2023 review of its properties and safety and a 2018 review of the compound. [2][3]

The accessory is not associated with documented harm in the sources reviewed. Sunless tanning reviews cite irritant or allergic contact dermatitis from DHA products and advise that tanners do not provide sun protection. [2][3]
Mitts are described in tanning routines as part of the standard kit with a self-tanning mousse or lotion, alongside exfoliation beforehand.

refs.title: Properties and safety of topical dihydroxyacetone in sunless tanning products: A review
